### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **10** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **281** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **24** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/rest/src/form-old-shape-before.json`, `packages/rest/vitest.repo-tests.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**78** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb854ea4d065c489e03a0d1b3b5bb9aeb8998626`.

⛔ **22** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **24** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/rest/src/form-old-shape-before.json`, `packages/rest/vitest.repo-tests.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_ERROR (literal, 39 pages)`
- **29** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **191** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb854ea4d065c489e03a0d1b3b5bb9aeb8998626` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5a6cf6a402fb36c424d66407cccfb9e99bb59481` — the merge of head `67af96fb676e6e2064098f83227d2aa3fab4c6c2` into base `cb854ea4d065c489e03a0d1b3b5bb9aeb8998626`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `claude/project-thread-pu5dnt` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5a6cf6a402fb36c424d66407cccfb9e99bb59481 && git checkout 5a6cf6a402fb36c424d66407cccfb9e99bb59481
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cb854ea4d065c489e03a0d1b3b5bb9aeb8998626 67af96fb676e6e2064098f83227d2aa3fab4c6c2 && git checkout -B drift-repro cb854ea4d065c489e03a0d1b3b5bb9aeb8998626 && git merge --no-ff 67af96fb676e6e2064098f83227d2aa3fab4c6c2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb854ea4d065c489e03a0d1b3b5bb9aeb8998626
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cb854ea4d065c489e03a0d1b3b5bb9aeb8998626` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

PR #37422 (PR B of card #37086's fixed cut), base = PR A's branch `claude/project-thread-pu5dnt`, 153 files, +4117 / -306, 14 commits. Read: the card body and its six comments, the PR body, the file list, the net diff against PR A's head, the check-runs on this head, ADR-0159 on `main`, and the cited code at this head. Nothing was built, run or ablated. The narrowing face holds, so every path of the diff is in the floor; `+` names the files the published hunks make a claim about.

**The security question of the brief, answered first.** No path that re-opens a withdrawn public form was found by reading. Traced: a `view` override's withdrawal against an authored `form`; a `form` override against an old-shape base; a base-withdrawn `form` item under a package-less or override old-shape row; rule 11 for the pair row and the package-less row; served rows only; the package-less list refusal at save, publish and restore; the door's own fallback read (S1). What follows is that the design reads closed, and that the card's proof of it is not in the PR: see M2.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change, named right or wrong.

- **`FormSchema`** (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`): a strict object of `name`, `object`, `label`, the body keys of `FormViewSchema` taken by reference less `data`, the protection and override-declaration fields; `data`, `viewKind`, `config`, `isDefault`, `order`, `scope` refused with guidance; the form-body refinement shared with the view (`checkFormViewBody`), the name-prefix check, the groups-into-sections fold. **Right** (D2, D3, ruled question 2 = A).
- **`defineForm`** declared again as the `form` type's factory. **Right** (ruled question 1 = A); it is absent on PR A's head and has one meaning here.
- **`form` as a metadata type**: enum member, registry row with `page`'s flags and `**/*.form.ts|yml|json`, type-to-schema map, `forms` stack collection, plural fold, owner stamp, `form: listed` in the customization package. **Right** (D1).
- **`forms` offers the array form only** (waivers in `scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs`). A dev-derived decision the card does not rule. **Right**: the name is `OBJECT.KEY` and is checked against `object`, so a map key would be a second spelling of the same identity.
- **`projectViewForms` / `projectedFormsOf`, the `_formDefinedIn` marker**: one projection of the three old shapes; the marker is stripped before the anonymous door answers (`formBodyOf`). **Right** (D5).
- **`formIntakeLayer` / `openFormAt`**: withdrawal by whole-item name over both types, closed links from unreadable bodies. **Right** (D6 rules 4 to 7).
- **`oldShapeFormWithdrawals`**: the exempt reader, with the required words in its docblock and its own anchor file; not registered as an ADR-0087 conversion. **Right** (item 6).
- **`FORM_ADDRESS_TAKEN`** in the error-code ledger. The code is **right**; the ledger comment that publishes where it is refused is **wrong** (M1).
- **The package-less list refusal**, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, at save, draft promotion and restore. **Right** (item 5), and it is the declared narrowing.
- **The override gate's "ships" read over both types** (`overrideWriteVerdict`). **Right** (item 5).
- **`/meta/form` read gate arms** (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`): `requiredPermissions` judged as for `view`. **Right**; the route pin the card asks for is missing (M2).
- **The `forms` translation family**: `label`, `description`, `title`, `submitBehavior` in a strict object. **Wrong against D8**, which lists a `sections` branch as part of the family (S3).
- **The door's second candidate source** (`servedForms.length` test in `form-routes.ts`). **Wrong** (S1).
- **`form` hidden from Studio's directory** (`HIDDEN_DIRECTORY_TYPES`). **Right**: ruled A in 7183329743.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/37086-form-metadata-type.md`: `minor` on `spec`, `metadata-protocol`, `rest`, `lint`, `metadata`, `metadata-core`, `objectql`, `runtime`, `cli`, `platform-objects`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. **Consistent** with AGENTS.md (a protocol kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves) and with the card's Done-when. The BREAKING banner names the export's new meaning and the refusal, the saves refused that are admitted today, and the one-line fix.
- **One ADR-0087 marker**: `registered form-type-define-form-and-packageless-list-at-form-name`, with its entry in `hits`. It covers the export and the refusal together, as the card asks. PR A's changeset carries its own single marker for the rename; see that record.
- `.changeset/37086-form-type-console-strings.md`: `patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Check Changeset` accepts it. Against the card's "`minor` on every package the diff moves" it is a deviation the seat should rule: S8.
- `@object-ui/types`: test files only, no changeset line. Right; the dev says so in the report.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1** (who adds the `forms` row to `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`): answered A in 7183329743. **Verified**: the skill's hunk is one line, the top-level key enumeration gains `` `forms`, `` and nothing else; no teaching text, example or eval. `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` raises the ceiling 6149 to 6151 and the arithmetic holds (24594 to 24603 priced bytes, a quarter rounded up is 6151): exactly the row's measured delta. The two rulings are cited in the script comment only, not in the PR body as the amendment asks: S9. The two cited records were not opened; they are outside this review's inputs, and the seat checks the citation.
- **Open question 2** (keep `form` hidden in Studio until card ③): answered A. **Verified** in `directoryScope.ts`.
- **`.claude/**`**: no path in the diff. Three gate-data edits are in it and are named for the seat, since each lets something through a check: the ratchet ceiling above; the `forms` waivers in `scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs`; and an allow-list entry `@object-ui/types:FormSchema` in `ui/scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` for a name collision with the spec's new `FormSchema`. Each carries its reason, none changes what an agent may do without the maintainer, so the header reads `none`.
- **The dev's out-of-scope finding on `sharing` credential marking** (class c): escalated by the seat. A security item is with the owner seat; no detail here.
- **The dev's `security_findings: withheld`**: not answered on the card. The seat collects it through the private channel; this review did not see it and cannot say it is covered by the findings below.
- **Other dev decisions surfaced for the seat:** `KNOWN_UNSEEDED` gains `form` in `metadata-create-seeds.test.ts`; `docs/qa/platform-checklist/coverage.json` waives `form` (S7); the liveness ledger `form.json` inherits `view`'s verdicts (N3).
- **Named, not made:** `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement` and `ui/docs/adr/0056` still name `defineForm` as the Studio helper; after this PR that is false twice over. ADR-0159:109 resolves again, onto a symbol with the opposite meaning of its sentence. All three are the seat's to order.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): a finding.** S5.
- **Check-runs on this head:** 67 runs, 60 success, 7 skipped, none red, none running. `Test Core` was still running when the review began and finished green. `Lint · docs & code guards` is green here, which is what restores PR A's red lane.

### ④ Design judgment

Against ADR-0159 D1 to D8, the ruled questions, and the card's Done-when. The tree was read, not the PR body's account.

M1 (must-fix) — **The address-clash refusal is judged at one door, and the published ledger says three.** `formAddressClashRefusal` has one call site, the save door (`protocol-save.ts`). Draft promotion and the restore writer ask the package-less list refusal and do not ask this one, and the holder read is of published forms. So a draft is not judged against another draft, a draft saved before a holder took the address is not judged again at publish, and a restore is not judged at all: each leaves two open forms on one address, which is the arrangement ruled question 3 = A refuses. Card item 7 names publish ("The `form` write door, `os validate` and publish each refuse") and Done-when asks a pin for each of the three refusals; there is no publish pin. The second comment on `FORM_ADDRESS_TAKEN` in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` says "the `form` save, draft promotion and restore doors refuse": declared, not enforced, in a `hits` file. Fix: ask the refusal in `promoteDraftForPublish` and the restore writer beside the list refusal, pin each, or correct the ledger and take the gap to the seat.

M2 (must-fix) — **Done-when's pins are not all there, and two of the eight D6 pins do not hold the read they name.** The card makes the pins the proof that no withdrawn form re-opens; a design that reads closed is not that proof.
  - By the PR's own table, ablation A2 (the `form` half of the layer) and A5f (the per-package `form` layer) turn nothing red, and pin 1 stays green under A1. The `form` half of the two-type layer is therefore unpinned: it can be deleted with the suite green. The card's fixture for pin 2 cannot show it, because the withdrawing override is itself the served candidate. A fixture that does: the base authors the `form` with its link kept and switched off, and an old-shape row of that name stands open on the same link; both doors must answer `404`. If the dev finds no fixture where that half is the only thing keeping an address closed, that is a finding for the seat (the half is dead), not a reason to leave it unpinned.
  - Absent: the served-rows-only pin, both fixtures. The closed-reading pin (a seeded package-less list, and a stored package-less container, over an authored form). In the bound pin: "where the base's pair cannot be ensured", "into the pair as its own item", and "after all of them the doors serve the package's form". The rule 9 pin (and see S6). The `declared_package_ships_no_such_item` pin for a `form` override of a name shipped in neither type. The route pin that a caller refused `/api/v1/meta/view/NAME` is refused `/api/v1/meta/form/NAME`. The reset and delete pins; the container re-saved without the member; the failed write that leaves both rows. Byte-equality of the list row (the one test asserts `viewKind`, on save only). The `data.object` door pin. The `GET /api/v1/meta/view` fixture pin. The `examples/app-crm` byte-equal pin. The pin that an old-shape `view` write on a taken slug still saves. The publish clash pin (M1).
  - Not in the PR: the per-type arm inventory of item 2; the ablation records for the D5 pins; the rebuild, on-disk mutation and empty-`git diff HEAD` proof Done-when asks of each ablation run.

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts`: `servedForms.length` being zero switches the door to `projectedFormsOf(views)`. That is a second candidate source inside the door, keyed on emptiness, where D6 rules 1 and 3 give the door one read, and it is a consumer-side fallback (Prime Directive 12). It was added for test doubles that answer an empty list. No divergence from the protocol's read was constructed, so it is not graded must-fix; key it on the protocol's capability or remove it and fix the doubles.

S2 (should-fix) — `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-form-reads.ts`: the cross-type served-row resolution runs only at addresses where the package authors a `form` item. Over a base that ships the form as an old shape, a package-less stored `form` row of the same name (a write the doors admit) is listed beside the base's projected form: two definitions at one address, against D5's "one address holds one definition" and its one served-row order. The answer also changes when the base later moves to `forms:`. It fails closed, so it is not a re-opening; it is an upgrade-time surprise. Scenario detail is in the summary to the seat.

S3 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`, `system/i18n-resolver.ts`: D8 lists `forms.NAME.sections.SECTION.label`, `.description` and `.fields.FIELD.*` as part of the family, with `_sections` as the default when the family has no key. The family schema is strict and refuses `sections`; `translateForm` reads section copy from `_sections` only. Add the branch, or have the seat name the card that owns it.

S4 (should-fix) — `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` and the protocol: `form` is overridable, and `translateForm` promises the ADR-0029 D9.2a rule that an override's own changed text outranks the base's catalog. There is no packaged-base accessor for `form` (no row in `PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS`), so the comparison has no base and an override's changed `title` is replaced by the base's translation, on `/meta/form` and on the public door.

S5 (should-fix, SQL first) — `readEffectiveForms` drops `names` and `packageId` from the request and filters in memory after full reads of both types and of every stored row of both. `readEffectiveFormItem` calls it up to three times for one by-name read, and each anonymous door request repeats the view-list and stored-row reads for the form read, the two per-package layers and the unreadable bodies. No reason is given in the code. Push the name and package predicates down, or state why the two-type resolution cannot.

S6 (should-fix) — Rule 9: Done-when asks a pin that an organization-scoped `form` save leaving a withdrawn form open is refused "as the same `view` save is today". On this tree no write-time withdrawal judgement exists in `metadata-protocol` (`anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn` has no caller there; `refuseOrganizationScopedWrite` refuses every organization-scoped write first). The PR neither pins the `form` case nor reports that the item's premise is stale. Report it to the seat with the reading.

S7 (should-fix) — `docs/qa/platform-checklist/coverage.json`: the waiver says no app the checklist drives authors `forms:`, and this diff adds `forms: [FeedbackForm]` to the showcase. It also names card ③ as the mover of contact-us where the card says ④.

S8 (should-fix) — the second changeset declares `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` at `patch` for two packages in a PR whose kind is `narrowed`. The gate is green; the card's sentence is not met to the letter. The seat rules whether the `@object-ui` train is exempt.

S9 (should-fix) — the PR body still lists the `SKILL.md` row under "named, not made" and does not cite the two rulings for the ceiling raise, which amendment 7183329743 asks for in the body. A body edit; it moves no head.

N1 (nit) — `packages/lint/src/validate-form-items.ts`: the consumer-less advisory is silent for every item that declares `overrides`, where D1 and item 9 ask it silent only when the base's form has a consumer.
N2 (nit) — `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`: `readEffectiveFormItem` answers the generic item when the name is listed only at another package; closed at this address, so no exposure.
N3 (nit) — `packages/spec/liveness/form.json` (`sharing`): the evidence quotes lines `findPublicForm` no longer has and names the `view` path for a `form` item.
N4 (nit) — `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts`: the registry-row comment says "overlayable per org" and names a scope set of global, org and user, while organization-scoped writes are refused on this tree (ADR-0131 D6); the comment describes a layer no door writes.
N5 (nit) — the cross-type resolution in `protocol-form-reads.ts` has no anchor file of its own; the doors' ADR-0159 anchor is an edit of the existing `form-routes.ts` file.

**Files that hold.** `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, `ui/form-intake-layer.ts`, `ui/anonymous-form-intake.ts`, `ui/old-shape-form-withdrawals.ts`, `ui/index.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `stack.zod.ts`, `kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts`, `kernel/customization-package.ts`, `kernel/collection-item-owner-stamp.ts`, `meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts`, `meta-spelling/meta-url-data.generated.ts`, the migration entry, `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`: each agrees with the decision it implements. `protocol-form-writes.ts` (the list refusal and the same-transaction row removal), `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, `runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, the two anchor files, `feedback.form.ts`: hold as read. Their findings are the ones graded above.

Two must-fix. The verdict is on M1 and M2; the nine should-fix items do not carry it.
